Truncating instead of rounding can give the physically wrong answer,. 

Consider this seesaw:
#_## 
. X

You're assuming that position 0 is the center of the first #. So the individual #s have their centers of mass at 0, 2, and 3, for an overall center of mass at 1.667.
The fulcrum is centered at 1, so it extends from 0.5 to 1.5. This is not balanced.
But if we truncate 1.667 down to 1, it appears perfectly centered over the fulcrum.

We could just as easily define position 0 as the left edge of the drawing, so that the masses extend from position 0 to 1, from 2 to 3, and from 3 to 4, while the fulcrum extends from 1 to 2. That puts the overall center of mass at 2.16667. It's still 0.1667 beyond the right edge of the fulcrum - changing the labeling system doesn't move the center of mass.

✅ Approved the contribution.
